title: Towards Robust and Generalized Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Noisy Label Learning
core_mechanism: adaptively routes likely clean examples through PEFT modules and bypasses suspected noisy examples
main_claim: protect PEFT modules from noisy interference while retaining parameter efficiency
mechanism_evidence: comparisons across PEFT methods and multiple synthetic noisy-label configurations
efficiency_reported: trainable parameters reported; complete wall-clock and scorer cost pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: substantial improvement over compared PEFT methods under noisy labels
reported_limitations: capacity that resists memorization can also impair clean-example learning; detailed compute assumptions pending full-text audit
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for PEFT clean routing"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official ACL long-paper page verifies title authors venue DOI and abstract. Full method appendix and cost extraction pending.

title: Fine tuning Pre trained Models for Robustness Under Noisy Labels
core_mechanism: first tunes a linear classifier to protect pretrained features then reduces the noisy subset and fine-tunes the full model
main_claim: efficiently transfer pretrained knowledge under noisy labels without relying on expensive conventional noisy-label pipelines
mechanism_evidence: analysis of pretrained-model behavior plus multi-benchmark comparison
efficiency_reported: efficiency is a stated objective; exact wall-clock VRAM and data-access accounting pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: reported improved denoising and classification across benchmarks
reported_limitations: two-stage procedure and subset-reduction assumptions require direct comparison with any proposed warm-up or filtering method
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for two-stage pretrained-model filtering"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. IJCAI proceedings page verifies formal publication. Also appears as arXiv 2310.17668.

title: Weed Out, Then Harvest: Dual Low-Rank Adaptation is an Effective Noisy Label Detector for Noise-Robust Learning
core_mechanism: uses separate clean/noisy LoRA modules; the noisy module acts as a sample-dependent threshold before downstream training
main_claim: decoupling noisy-label detection from classifier training avoids the feedback loop of small-loss selection
mechanism_evidence: noise-detection and classification experiments on synthetic and real noisy text datasets
efficiency_reported: reports parameter and memory overhead; full selection and external relabeling cost pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: reported accuracy gains over standard LoRA under multiple noise levels
reported_limitations: Findings not CCF-A full; later relabeling may use an external LLM; dual modules add memory and training stages
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for dual-adapter noise detection"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official ACL Findings page verifies status; must not be described as ACL main-conference full paper.

title: Why LoRA Resists Label Noise: A Theoretical Framework for Noise-Robust Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
core_mechanism: derives rank-dependent memorization and optimal-rank relations and exploits temporal separation through rank discrepancy
main_claim: LoRA rank limits noisy-label memorization and lower optimal rank is predicted as noise increases
mechanism_evidence: theorems plus noise-detection and classification experiments
efficiency_reported: trainable rank discussed; full wall-clock memory and two-adapter cost pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: reported strong noise-detection F1 and retained task accuracy
reported_limitations: single-author preprint; assumptions and theorem-to-deep-network transfer require scrutiny; RACT uses two adapters
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for rank scheduling rank discrepancy and PEFT temporal noise detection"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. arXiv metadata resolved separately; publication remains preprint.

title: Compute-Constrained Data Selection
extra_models: selection model or metric may vary
core_mechanism: defines a cost-aware utility that trades data-selection cost against downstream fine-tuning gain across model and token budgets
main_claim: expensive perplexity and gradient selectors are often not compute-optimal; cheap alternatives can dominate
mechanism_evidence: large sweeps over selection compute model-size ratios and fine-tuning tokens
efficiency_reported: selection and training compute are both in the objective
strongest_result: reports compute-optimal regimes including required training-to-selection model-size ratios

direct_prior_risk: high:"critical direct prior for counting selector cost inside fixed-budget training"

title: Computational Budget Should Be Considered in Data Selection
core_mechanism: bilevel inner training plus outer selection optimization
main_claim: probabilistically reparameterizes budget-conditioned subset selection and avoids Hessian and full inner-loop solutions
mechanism_evidence: bilevel objective plus experiments across budgets and modalities
efficiency_reported: compute budget is explicit; full optimizer overhead and single-GPU feasibility pending full paper
strongest_result: reports gains up to 14.42 percent over compared selectors
reported_limitations: not designed for low-quality-data defect identification; bilevel optimization may be too costly for the local regime
direct_prior_risk: high:"critical direct prior for budget-conditioned allocation"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official NeurIPS main-track page verifies publication.

title: MATES: Model-Aware Data Selection for Efficient Pretraining with Data Influence Models
core_mechanism: locally probes the changing learner to collect oracle influence and continually updates a small model that selects currently useful data
main_claim: model-aware dynamic selection improves pretraining efficiency over static quality rules or fixed reference models
mechanism_evidence: online influence-model training and pretraining experiments
efficiency_reported: selection-model and probing costs exist; exact accounting pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: reported more effective pretraining data selection than static alternatives
reported_limitations: large-scale pretraining setting and auxiliary influence model may not transfer economically to one GPU
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for time-varying learned sample utility"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official NeurIPS main-track page verifies publication.

title: Handling Label Noise via Instance-Level Difficulty Modeling and Dynamic Optimization
core_mechanism: collects wrong-event histories to model both cleanliness and difficulty then applies probabilistic dynamic weighting
main_claim: instance-level dynamic optimization can improve robustness while reducing tuning storage and compute relative to prior noisy-label pipelines
mechanism_evidence: six synthetic and real noisy-label benchmarks
efficiency_reported: reports nearly 75 percent reduction in storage and computational time; absolute wall-clock pending extraction
strongest_result: reported state-of-the-art performance on six benchmarks
reported_limitations: two-stage training and history collection remain costs; defect coverage is primarily label noise
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for low-cost joint cleanliness-difficulty scoring"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official NeurIPS main-track page verifies publication and code link.

title: Enhancing Sample Selection Against Label Noise by Cutting Mislabeled Easy Examples
core_mechanism: uses a later training state to recalibrate an early confident subset and remove mislabeled-easy examples
main_claim: mislabeled examples that are predicted correctly early can be more harmful than other mislabeled data and require targeted removal
mechanism_evidence: CIFAR WebVision and full ImageNet-1k experiments
efficiency_reported: selection-history and recalibration cost pending full-text extraction
strongest_result: reported improved selection and model performance through fewer mislabeled-easy examples
reported_limitations: focuses on label noise; later-state recalibration may delay usable selection decisions
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for separating difficulty from harmful mislabeled-easy behavior"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. Official NeurIPS main-track page verifies publication.

title: Debiased Sample Selection for Learning with Noisy Labels
core_mechanism: adjusts class-level marginal selection and uses candidate-class dynamics to avoid both easy-class and spuriously-low-loss confirmation bias
main_claim: plug-in debiasing improves existing selectors while preserving hard samples and preventing wrong-label memorization
mechanism_evidence: CIFAR-N Clothing1M WebVision and synthetic-noise experiments plus trajectory analysis
efficiency_reported: plug-in overhead pending full paper and supplement extraction
strongest_result: reported consistent gains when added to existing selectors and advanced LNL pipelines
reported_limitations: limited to classification label noise; dependence on uniform-target adjustment may interact with real imbalance
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for hard-clean preservation and confirmation-bias correction"
audit_notes: Search date 2026-07-31. CVF official page verifies CVPR full-paper status and code.

title: What is Your Data Worth to GPT? LLM-Scale Data Valuation with Influence Functions
core_mechanism: uses backpropagation structure for efficient gradient projection in influence-function data valuation
main_claim: influence estimation can scale to billion-parameter models and billion-token data with large throughput and memory improvements

efficiency_reported: reports up to 6500 times throughput and five times memory improvement
strongest_result: competitive valuation accuracy at substantially reduced compute and memory
reported_limitations: targets attribution and valuation rather than online noisy-data allocation; still raises a strong efficient-influence baseline
direct_prior_risk: high:"direct prior for efficient gradient-based sample value estimation"
